answer: A sybil farm chases one nectar: voting weight. Gate it behind airworthiness. Each identity must hold the airworthiness certificate of one amateur-built aircraft: plans filed, airframe inspected, 40 test hours logged with its transponder signal on record. One certificate backs one identity; the registry rejects a second claim on the same airframe. Each fake costs 8,000 units and 150 days, so 100 fakes cost 800,000 units and 15,000 days. Cheapest cheat: a finished kit aircraft for 12,000 units, but the seller surrenders its own certificate, and a forged umber primer batch fails the log check.
